messages:
oliver: weird one - our python async client fails intermittently when running inside corp network with an HTTPS proxy that does TLS interception. sync client is fine. anyone seen proxy + custom CA issues?

emily: what does "fails intermittently" mean? full trace?

oliver: sometimes on first request it works, then next request throws `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed` coming out of httpx when it tries to reuse a pooled connection. stack points at httpcore connection open.

kevin: are you using HTTPS_PROXY pointing at a proxy that terminates TLS (so the proxy presents its own cert)? or is it plain http proxy?

oliver: HTTPS_PROXY=https://corp-proxy.internal:443 (proxy does TLS and signs with corp CA). I set SSL_CERT_FILE and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE to /etc/pki/corp-ca.pem. Sync requests client honors it. Async fails only when using our AsyncClient wrapper.

maria: couple of axes here: (1) trust for proxy TLS vs trust for destination; (2) httpx/httpcore pooling + SSLContext reuse; (3) SDK wrapper constructing SSLContext itself (certifi-only) and not using env or provided cert file.

emily: also check `trust_env` flag. httpx will read HTTPS_PROXY env when trust_env is True. Our AsyncClient wrapper currently sets `trust_env=False` in the transport to avoid surprising behaviour for hosted users. If trust_env=False and you pass proxies manually we might be creating a transport that ignores SSL_CERT_FILE.

oliver: interesting — we do set trust_env=False to avoid leaking proxies in hosted infra. but for Dedicated/Private we should probably default to True or at least expose it. the intermittent nature seems tied to connection reuse: first connection builds a context somehow that picks up the CA, pooled one doesn't.

kevin: i dug into code quickly: async constructor builds an ssl.SSLContext and calls `context.load_verify_locations(certifi.where())`. it doesn't check env or accept ca_bundle. sync path uses requests and honors SSL_CERT_FILE. so parity bug + missing trust_env param.

maria: repro note from local: using raw httpx.AsyncClient(verify='/etc/pki/corp-ca.pem', trust_env=True, proxies={'https': 'https://corp-proxy.internal:443'}) works consistently. our wrapper without `verify` and `trust_env=True` fails after a couple requests.

oliver: workaround for us: create raw httpx.AsyncClient and pass to the SDK internals or monkeypatch _transport. but that's ugly. would prefer SDK to accept `verify`, `ca_bundle`, and `trust_env` on AsyncClient and forward proxies correctly.

emily: agree. API suggestion: AsyncClient(..., ca_bundle: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None, trust_env: Optional[bool] = None, proxies: Optional[Mapping[str,str]] = None). semantics: explicit ca_bundle > SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE env > certifi; for Dedicated if base_url is private and env proxies present, default trust_env=True. document this behavior.

kevin: typing note: our typed stubs currently don't include these params for async. that causes mypy errors and people try `**kwargs` which we swallow. add explicit types in stubs so autocomplete shows `ca_bundle` and `trust_env`. also add overloads that accept httpx transport types for advanced users.

maria: retry behavior: when proxy TLS fails we should not retry by default. we currently have retry-on-transport-errors which retries on some SSLErrors and leads to confusing waterfall. suggest `retry_on_ssl=False` default and doc explanation for corporate proxy edgecases.

oliver: perfect. if you add `trust_env` toggle, we can keep hosted default False and Dedicated default True so customers behind corporate proxies have a smoother path.

ci-bot: opened issue #5544: "py-sdk async: proxy + custom CA parity - expose ca_bundle, trust_env, proxies; typing + disable ssl retries by default" linking this thread.

kevin: i'll take this. plan: small additive API changes to AsyncClient (ca_bundle, trust_env, proxies), make AsyncClient prefer explicit ca_bundle then env then certifi, ensure pooled SSLContext respects provided CA, and change retry middleware so SSLCertVerificationError is non-retriable. add unit tests + mypy tests + a Dedicated docs example showing systemd/k8s env and an httpx troubleshooting one-liner.

emily: minor perf/regression note: ensure creating per-host SSLContext doesn't explode memory; reuse contexts keyed by verify path. also include a short example in README showing how to run with HTTPS proxy and custom CA: ```bash
export HTTPS_PROXY=https://corp-proxy.internal:443
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/pki/corp-ca.pem
python - <<'PY'
from redwood import AsyncClient
import asyncio
client = AsyncClient(api_key='x', base_url='https://redwood.dedicated.internal', trust_env=True)
asyncio.run(client.generate('hi'))
PY
```

maria: thanks Kevin, ping here when PR is up and we'll smoke test with our corp proxy. this will save a lot of dedicated customers from weird intermittent failures.

oliver: thanks all — workaround stands but excited for the proper fix. :rocket:
